who: William Allen Brown, historian of West Africa at the University of Wisconsin–Madison, PhD in African history there.

evidence.says: Lists Janet Ewald's Taqali dissertation, 1982–1983, with adviser Brown, William A.
Identifies William Allen Brown as a Wisconsin PhD in African history and a professor of West African history in the department for over thirty years.
The candidate item identifies William Wells Brown, the nineteenth-century novelist, playwright and historian, and links LC n80033934.

notes: The supervisor is William Allen Brown, not candidate p-1426, William Wells Brown.

who: William R. Emerson, Yale history faculty member and military historian in the 1950s.

evidence.says: The 1956 report identifies William R. Emerson as an assistant professor of history at Yale who would teach military history since World War I.

The candidate authority is W. Eric Emerson, also William Eric Emerson, University of Alabama PhD and South Carolina Historical Society executive director; its sources include his 2002 dissertation Sons of privilege.

notes: The Yale military historian is distinct from candidate p-5017, William Eric Emerson. The Flammer supervision itself was supplied by AHA.

who: Robert Sonné Cohen, Boston University professor of physics and philosophy and co-supervisor of Joan Bromberg's Wisconsin doctorate.

evidence.says: Lists Joan Lisa Bromberg, Maxwell's Concept of Electric Displacement, University of Wisconsin, 1967, with Robert S Cohen as second supervisor alongside Erwin Hiebert.
The authority identifies Cohen, R. S. (Robert Sonné), with usage Robert S. Cohen, as a physicist, philosopher and professor of physics and philosophy at Boston University.
Identifies R. S. Cohen, also Robert Sonné Cohen, as a physicist and philosopher of science employed by Boston University, with LC n50026516.
The other candidate is the historian Robert Cohen associated with When the old left was young, a Berkeley history PhD in 1987 and a University of Georgia faculty member.

notes: Direct student, thesis, university and year agreement identifies p-125410; p-100815 is a different historian. A Wisconsin faculty appointment is not required for this co-supervision.

who: André Charbonneau, AHA-listed adviser of Marie-Hélène Vallée's 2006 Laval dissertation on Grosse-Île workers.

evidence.says: The candidate authority identifies André Charbonneau as the author of The fortifications of Ile aux Noix (1994).
The corresponding government catalogue record identifies André Charbonneau as a Parks Canada historian.
The Grosse-Île episode bibliography credits André Charbonneau with La station de quarantaine de la Grosse-Île (1987) and, with André Sévigny, 1847, Grosse Île (1997).
Confirms Vallée's dissertation title, Université Laval, 2006, and links the university repository record.

notes: Candidate p-134078 is plausible by name and Grosse-Île expertise, but no permitted source accessed independently connects that historian to this supervision. The university repository could not be read; thesis full text remains unread.

who: Patrice Gueniffey, EHESS directeur d'études specializing in the French Revolution and Empire.

evidence.says: Identifies Patrice Gueniffey as a historian and EHESS directeur d'études, associated with Bonaparte and 1814 : la campagne de France.
The EHESS Annuaire for 2006 identifies Patrice Gueniffey as directeur d'études teaching Histoire de la Révolution française.
The publisher identifies Philippe Münch as the author of a political-studies doctorate completed at EHESS in cotutelle with Université Laval.
Münch's author biography confirms doctorates in history and political studies from Laval and EHESS and postdoctoral work beginning in 2008.

notes: The AHA adviser matches the candidate's exact name, specialist field and EHESS role. The student's EHESS–Laval cotutelle explains the Laval listing; no Laval faculty appointment is inferred. Independent supervision documentation was not accessible.

who: John N. Dickinson, historian at Miami University from 1965, PhD Wisconsin 1968, author of To Build a Canal.

evidence.says: Miami's faculty memorial identifies John N. Dickinson, Wisconsin PhD 1968, appointed in history at Miami in 1965 and promoted to associate professor in 1973; it notes that he directed a PhD dissertation.

The candidate authority identifies John Alexander Dickinson, author of Justice et justiciables and A short history of Quebec, teaching Quebec history at Université de Montréal; it records a Toronto doctorate and a Montréal appointment in 1980.

notes: The Miami supervisor is distinct from candidate p-2013, John Alexander Dickinson of Montréal.

who: Peter Wayne Farrugia, Wilfrid Laurier historian of modern Europe, war and pacifism, DPhil Oxford 1991.

evidence.says: Kyle Falcon's 2019 history PhD dissertation record names Peter Farrugia as first adviser, with the role Supervisor.
Peter Wayne Farrugia's CV records a 1991 Oxford DPhil in modern history, Laurier employment from 1997, and Religious Pacifism in Britain among his publications.
The candidate authority cites Religious pacifism in Britain and identifies Peter Farrugia as an Oxford PhD who taught in Ottawa.

notes: Direct supervision evidence, matching Oxford doctorate and matching publication connect the Laurier supervisor to the candidate authority.

who: John F. Hall, Brigham Young University professor of classical languages and ancient history, doctorate Pennsylvania.

evidence.says: Identifies John F. Hall as BYU professor of classical languages and ancient history, a scholar of Roman history, with a Pennsylvania doctorate and twenty-nine years on the BYU faculty by 2007.
Candidate John R. Hall is a sociologist at Missouri and later UC Davis, with a University of Washington PhD.
Candidate John W. (John William) Hall is the Wisconsin–Madison military historian associated with Uncommon defense.
Candidate John A. Hall is a sociologist at Southampton and McGill with a 1976 London School of Economics PhD.
Candidate John Whitney Hall is the historian of premodern Japan at Michigan and Yale, associated with Japanese history and Japan in the Muromachi age.

notes: The BYU Roman historian's name, institution and field distinguish him from all four candidates: p-127266, p-144545, p-133182 and p-2414. The Draper supervision itself was supplied by AHA.
